title: Internal: handling procedure for a post-issuance correction that requires the originals back
content:
## Situation this procedure covers

This runbook of the Bills of Lading and Transport Documents product applies to an issued paper transport document on a document type whose tier requires the originals to be returned before an issued document is corrected, when all of the following hold during the contact:

- the documentation party has a correction request on file for a particular that the tier still allows to be corrected;
- the originals of the set in force are still in circulation;
- the shipper printed on the document, being the documentation party holding the record, has those originals with it at the line's origin office.

When the procedure is complete, the originals of the old set are recorded as lodged at the origin office, the particular reads as requested and the request is completed, the correction fee of the request is on the documentation account, and the corrected document is in force as the next set with its originals in circulation again.

## Formal steps

1. **Lodge the originals** (performed by the customer themselves, the printed shipper acting as documentation party): return_originals_for_correction_b9bd03b3. The outstanding originals of the set in force are lodged at the origin office.
2. **Apply the correction** (agent): apply_particular_correction_a24e9121. The requested particular is rewritten and the correction request completed.
3. **Book the correction fee** (agent): charge_correction_fee_18211c73. The correction fee of the executed request is booked.
4. **Issue the corrected set** (agent): issue_corrected_set_a7062696. The corrected document is issued as the next set and its originals are put into circulation.

## Role table

| Step | Performed by | Business object changed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The customer themselves | Documentation history: originals recorded as lodged at the origin office |
| 2 | Agent | Printed particular of the document; correction request completed |
| 3 | Agent | Documentation account: correction fee of the request |
| 4 | Agent | Set in force, date of issue and originals in circulation |

## What each step hands to the next

- Step 1 fixes the transport document on which the lodgement was recorded; that same document is the one corrected in step 2 and reissued in step 4.
- Step 2 hands its transport document to step 3, which charges that document.
- Step 3 hands the correction request it charged to step 4, as the request the corrected set carries.

## Why the order is fixed

- **Lodging before applying the correction.** On a tier that requires the originals back, a correction is applied only after every outstanding original has been returned, so that none remain outstanding. Applied first, the correction would rewrite a document whose old originals are still in circulation, which that gate forbids.
- **Applying before booking the fee.** A correction request is charged once it has been executed, and each request is charged once. Booked first, the fee would charge a correction that does not yet stand on the document, whereas on these tiers the fee is booked only for a correction already standing on the document.
- **Booking the fee before issuing the corrected set.** The corrected set is issued only once the correction fee of the request it carries has been booked. Issued first, the set would leave the desk with its documentation account incomplete; the fee step also hands the corrected set the request it carries.

## The lodgement and the timing of the contact

The lodgement is the printed shipper's own act, taken from the documentation party only when it is that shipper, and performed at the line's origin office during the same contact with the originals it has there. When the originals are not at the origin office during the contact, the procedure does not start, and the request waits, within its return deadline, for a later contact. Every other step is a record change the desk completes at once; no step waits on a delivery, a payment clearing, an outside approval or the passing of time.

## Counter-examples of reordering

| Swap | What would go wrong |
|---|---|
| Correction applied before the lodgement | The document would be rewritten while old originals are still in circulation |
| Fee booked before the correction is applied | The fee would charge a correction not yet standing on the document |
| Corrected set issued before the fee is booked | The set would leave with an incomplete documentation account and without the request handed on by the fee step |
